title: Retrieval Augmented Time Series Forecasting (RAF)
key_mechanism: Retrieves related historical windows from a fixed corpus built from training data and fuses them (attention-based) into a Chronos-style TS foundation model at inference; retrieval index is built once and never updated online.
evaluation_datasets: Multiple public TS domains (via Chronos zero-shot benchmark suite)
notes: Database construction is static/offline; no mechanism to add, decay or evict entries as new data arrives post-deployment.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Models for Time Series Forecasting (RATD)
key_mechanism: Embedding-based retrieval of most-relevant historical series from a database (built from the full training split) to guide a conditional diffusion denoiser; reference-guided diffusion process.
evaluation_datasets: Electricity, weather, exchange-rate, ETT and other standard multivariate TS benchmarks
notes: Read pp.1-5 in full text: retrieval database = entire training set, indexed once before training; no discussion of drift, database updating, or memory eviction after deployment.

title: TimeRAF: Retrieval-Augmented Foundation model for Zero-shot Time Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Learnable end-to-end retriever over a domain-specific 'time series knowledge base'; Channel Prompting fuses retrieved series along channel dimension into a TS foundation model for zero-shot forecasting.
notes: Read pp.1-4: knowledge base is explicitly constructed once from available historical data with de-duplication ('no overlap present in the data within the knowledge base'); no online maintenance policy discussed.

title: TS-RAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Time Series Foundation Models are Stronger Zero-Shot Forecaster
key_mechanism: Pretrained TS encoder retrieves semantically relevant segments from a fixed knowledge base; Adaptive Retrieval Mixer (ARM) fuses retrieved patterns with the TSFM's own representation without fine-tuning.
evaluation_datasets: Seven public benchmark datasets across domains
notes: Full text confirms knowledge base is fixed/offline per dataset; ARM adapts fusion weights per query but the retrieval corpus itself is never updated, pruned or evicted over time.

title: MemDA: Forecasting Urban Time Series with Memory-based Drift Adaptation
key_mechanism: Learnable parametric 'Pattern Memory' matrix (key-value style, not raw segment storage) queried via attention; a meta-dynamic network conditions forecasts on drift signals and periodicity without retraining, avoiding recomputation of the whole model.
evaluation_datasets: Urban time series: traffic speed/flow, metro/taxi demand
notes: Full text confirms memory is a fixed-size trainable parameter matrix updated by gradient descent jointly with the forecaster, not an explicit growing/evictable instance database; no utility-based retention or fault-contamination handling; domain is urban mobility, not industrial machinery.

title: Stationarity-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Time Series Forecasting (SARAF)
key_mechanism: Diversity-aware candidate selection over a similarity-based candidate pool, with diversification strength modulated by dataset-level stationarity; stationarity-aware aggregation of retrieved futures.
notes: Directly targets non-stationarity in retrieval-augmented forecasting (closest topical match to G3a/e), but per abstract addresses selection/aggregation at query time from a pool, not online growth/eviction of the pool itself as new post-deployment data arrives.

title: Not All Retrievals are Useful: Cross-Attention for Input-Aware RAG in Time Series Forecasting (Cross-RAG)
key_mechanism: Query-retrieval cross-attention selectively weights retrieved samples by input-level relevance, reducing sensitivity to the number of retrieved k and to irrelevant retrievals; model-agnostic.
evaluation_datasets: Multiple TSFM backbones and RAG baselines/benchmarks
notes: Addresses relevance-filtering at fusion time, not maintenance of the retrieval database over time; database remains static.

title: Model-agnostic Retrieval-Augmented Extended Forecasting (RAEF)
key_mechanism: Refines RAF: retrieves directly in input-space (not embedding-space) and aggregates by concatenation (preserving temporal structure) rather than averaging.
notes: Efficiency/accuracy refinement of retrieval and fusion, not database maintenance under drift; explicitly built on and compared to RAF.

title: Spectral Retrieval-Augmented Time-Series Forecasting (SpecReTF)
key_mechanism: Retrieves via frequency-domain (spectral) similarity instead of time-domain distance; applies an exponential moving-average recency weighting scheme over historical windows to balance recency and history.
notes: Recency-weighting is a simple fixed decay applied at retrieval-scoring time, not a learned/feedback-driven utility-based eviction policy; no discussion of recurring regimes or fault contamination.

title: Retrieval Based Time Series Forecasting (ReTime)
key_mechanism: Two-stage relational retrieval + content synthesis; theoretical analysis connecting retrieval to MSE uncertainty reduction under long-horizon forecasting.
notes: Established early (2022) precedent for the general retrieval-forecasting idea, static-database setting; no drift/maintenance treatment.

title: RATSF: Empowering Customer Service Volume Management through Retrieval-Augmented Time-Series Forecasting
key_mechanism: Time Series Knowledge Base (TSKB) with an indexing system, and a Retrieval-Augmented Cross-Attention (RACA) transformer-decoder module for retrieving key historical segments under acknowledged non-stationarity.
evaluation_datasets: Fliggy hotel service call-volume data, other domains
notes: Explicitly targets non-stationary retrieval but the TSKB is built and indexed once; no discussion of continual updating post-deployment.

title: RAF-LLM: a retrieval-augmented large language model framework for remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery
key_mechanism: Degradation-specific external knowledge base of historical run-to-failure trajectories; learnable dual-branch retriever with prediction-oriented alignment feeds an LLM-based RUL regressor.
evaluation_datasets: Rotating-machinery run-to-failure degradation datasets (e.g. bearing/turbofan-style RUL benchmarks)
notes: Directly on machine data (RUL of rotating machinery) and uses a historical-trajectory memory bank, but the knowledge base is a fixed run-to-failure corpus (offline, complete degradation histories) rather than an online-maintained, drift-evolving memory of a currently-deployed unit; no eviction/utility policy described in abstract.

title: Probabilistic Weather Prediction with an Analog Ensemble
key_mechanism: Analog Ensemble (AnEn): for each new forecast, finds the historical instances (analogs) most similar to the current deterministic forecast trajectory and uses their observed outcomes to build a probabilistic forecast; the analog database is the full historical record.
notes: Canonical kNN/analog forecasting method; database is static historical record, not maintained/evicted online; foundational for the analog-ensemble line extended below to wind/solar.

title: A novel application of an analog ensemble for short-term wind power forecasting
key_mechanism: Applies analog ensemble method to wind power forecasting: retrieves historical analog situations from an NWP/observation archive to construct an empirical predictive distribution for turbine power output.
notes: Machine-adjacent (wind turbine power forecasting) analog/kNN method; database is the fixed historical archive, not actively pruned/updated for regime drift; no fault-contamination safeguard discussed.

title: An analog ensemble for short-term probabilistic solar power forecast
key_mechanism: Analog ensemble applied to solar power forecasting using historical NWP-observation pairs as the analog database.
notes: Same static-database analog approach as above, applied to solar generation equipment.

title: A comparative study of just-in-time-learning based methods for online soft sensor modeling
key_mechanism: Comparative survey of JITL (lazy-learning) soft-sensor methods: for every new query, a local model is built from the k most similar historical samples retrieved from a maintained database; compares similarity criteria and database designs.
notes: Foundational JITL survey; establishes the 'query -> retrieve similar historical samples -> local model' paradigm equivalent in spirit to the proposed thesis design, but for shallow (PLS/regression) models and single-step soft-sensor prediction, not deep multivariate multi-horizon forecasters.

title: Just-in-Time Kernel Learning with Adaptive Parameter Selection for Soft Sensor Modeling of Batch Processes
key_mechanism: JITL with kernel learning and adaptively selected local-model hyperparameters per query.
notes: Adaptive local-model complexity within JITL, not database maintenance per se.

title: Adaptive Gaussian Mixture Model-Based Relevant Sample Selection for JITL Soft Sensor Development
key_mechanism: Proposes a GMM-based similarity/relevance criterion (instead of simple distance) for selecting which historical samples in the database are relevant to a query, handling non-Gaussian, time-varying process behavior.
evaluation_datasets: Numerical example + industrial process case study
notes: Directly about which historical samples should be treated as 'relevant' for retrieval — closely related to a utility/relevance-scoring policy, but the relevance criterion is a fixed statistical similarity measure, not learned from delayed forecast-error feedback, and there is no explicit eviction/decay mechanism nor treatment of fault-contaminated samples.

title: Adaptive soft sensor modeling framework based on just-in-time learning and kernel partial least squares regression for nonlinear multiphase batch processes
key_mechanism: Combines JITL with kernel PLS for multiphase batch processes to adapt to nonlinearity.
notes: Model-side adaptation; database handling is standard JITL windowing.

title: A Probabilistic Just-in-Time Learning Framework for Soft Sensor Development With Missing Data
key_mechanism: Probabilistic JITL formulation that tolerates missing entries in the historical database when selecting relevant samples.
notes: Handles data-quality issues (missingness) in the retrieval database, related to but distinct from the fault-contamination protection question (G3d), which concerns admitting anomalous/faulty — not merely missing — data as valid analogues.

title: Semisupervised JITL Framework for Nonlinear Industrial Soft Sensing Based on Locally Semisupervised Weighted PCR
key_mechanism: Semi-supervised JITL leveraging unlabeled historical samples in the database alongside labeled ones for local model construction.
notes: Extends JITL sample pool to unlabeled data; not directly about eviction/drift maintenance.

title: Supervised local and non-local structure preserving projections with application to just-in-time learning for adaptive soft sensor
key_mechanism: Dimensionality-reduction technique used as a similarity/relevance measure for JITL sample selection.
notes: Representation-learning side of JITL similarity measures; peripheral to database-maintenance policy question.

title: Integrating adaptive moving window and just-in-time learning paradigms for soft-sensor design
key_mechanism: Combines an adaptive moving-window database (recency-based forgetting, window size adapted to process change rate) with JITL relevant-sample retrieval for soft-sensor design under time-varying conditions.
evaluation_datasets: Industrial soft-sensor benchmark process(es) (per title/venue; full text paywalled)
notes: Title/venue indicate this is squarely a 'database maintenance under drift' JITL paper (adaptive moving window = a time-decay/eviction policy). Full text was not accessible (no OA copy found via Unpaywall/OpenAlex); abstract text also unavailable through OpenAlex. Verification limited to metadata (title, venue, DOI, year) confirmed via OpenAlex API — treat as the single most directly on-point piece of prior art for G3c and re-verify manually before writing the proposal.

title: A deep learning just-in-time modeling approach for soft sensor based on variational autoencoder
key_mechanism: Uses a VAE-learned latent representation as the similarity space for JITL sample retrieval, i.e. a 'deep JITL' variant.
notes: Closest JITL paper to 'deep retrieval embeddings' asked about in G3c, but still single-target soft-sensor regression (not multivariate multi-horizon forecasting) and does not address recurring-regime handling or fault-contamination of the database.

title: Online-Dynamic-Clustering-Based Soft Sensor for Industrial Semi-Supervised Data Streams
key_mechanism: Dynamically clusters incoming streaming process data into evolving clusters (proxy for regimes) to maintain an adaptive soft-sensor database under streaming/semi-supervised conditions.
notes: 2023, dynamic/streaming database maintenance in the soft-sensor JITL tradition; relevant recent evidence that database-maintenance-under-drift work continues but still targeted at single-output regression, not deep multi-horizon forecasting.

title: The role of artificial intelligence-driven soft sensors in advanced sustainable process industries: A critical review
key_mechanism: Recent (2023) critical review of AI-driven soft sensors including adaptive/JITL approaches for process industries.
notes: Useful up-to-date survey entry point confirming JITL/adaptive soft-sensor remains an active but narrow (regression, shallow-to-medium depth models) sub-field as of 2023.

title: Gradient based sample selection for online continual learning
key_mechanism: Selects replay-buffer samples to maximize gradient-based diversity, formulated as a constrained optimization (surrogate to facility location), for online continual learning of classifiers.
notes: General replay-buffer selection method transferable in principle to TS memory retention, but not TS/forecasting-specific and not evaluated on machine data.

title: Online Class-Incremental Continual Learning with Adversarial Shapley Value
key_mechanism: Uses Shapley-value-based utility scores to decide which buffer samples to retain/replace in online class-incremental replay.
notes: Utility-based buffer management analogous in spirit to G3b's 'utility = forecast-error contribution' idea, but for classification, not regression/forecasting; no TS or machine data.

title: Continual Prototype Evolution: Learning Online from Non-Stationary Data Streams
key_mechanism: Maintains an evolving set of class prototypes with a self-supervised replay/pseudo-prototype mechanism as data streams non-stationarily.
notes: Prototype-bank maintenance under non-stationarity, transferable concept but classification-focused, not TS forecasting.

title: AdaER: An adaptive experience replay approach for continual lifelong learning
key_mechanism: Adaptive experience-replay sample scoring/retrieval mechanism for continual lifelong learning.
notes: General continual-learning replay adaptation; not TS-specific.

title: Dark Experience for General Continual Learning: a Strong, Simple Baseline
key_mechanism: Reservoir-sampling-based replay buffer combined with knowledge-distillation-style logit matching as a strong general continual-learning baseline.
notes: Reservoir sampling is the canonical simple eviction baseline referenced by G3f-adjacent memory-management comparisons; not TS-specific.

title: MemStream: Memory-Based Streaming Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Maintains a fixed-size memory of 'normal' encoded records for streaming anomaly detection, with drift-aware memory updates; scores incoming records by distance to memory.
evaluation_datasets: Multiple streaming anomaly-detection benchmarks (incl. some sensor/industrial streams)
notes: Already mapped by user as prior art on the anomaly-detection side; relevant here as an existing memory-update mechanism whose explicit fault/anomaly exclusion criterion (memory update gated by low anomaly score) is directly analogous to the contamination-protection idea in G3d, but applied to a normality memory for detection, not a forecasting-analogue memory.

title: METER: A Dynamic Concept Adaptation Framework for Online Anomaly Detection
key_mechanism: Dynamic concept-adaptation framework for online anomaly detection (already mapped by user).
notes: Already known to user; included for completeness/cross-reference only.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
key_mechanism: Neural long-term memory module that learns to memorize historical context at test time via a surprise-based update rule, integrated with attention as short-term memory; general sequence modeling architecture (not TS-forecasting-specific in evaluation).
evaluation_datasets: Language modeling, genomics, time series, and other sequence benchmarks
notes: The long-term/short-term memory split matches the thesis's LTM/STM framing conceptually, but Titans' memory is a parametric neural module updated by a fixed learned surprise-gradient rule — it is not an explicit, inspectable segment database with a discrete retention/eviction/regime-reuse policy, and it is not evaluated on industrial machine data or under deployment-time distribution shift specifically.

title: A survey on long short-term memory networks for time series prediction
key_mechanism: Survey of LSTM-family architectures for TS prediction.
notes: Background/context only; not about external/retrieval memory.

title: KNN Classifier with Self Adjusting Memory for Heterogeneous Concept Drift (SAM-kNN)
key_mechanism: Maintains two explicit memories (short-term / long-term) of labeled instances for kNN classification; short-term memory retains only currently-relevant instances (recent, consistent with current concept), long-term memory compresses and retains knowledge of past concepts for potential reuse; includes an explicit compression/cleaning procedure to keep long-term memory consistent, directly enabling recurring-concept reuse.
evaluation_datasets: Standard concept-drift stream classification benchmarks (synthetic + real, e.g. weather, electricity)
notes: The single closest conceptual precedent for the thesis's LTM/STM split and for G3e (recurring regimes): SAM-kNN explicitly keeps and reuses old-concept memory rather than purely evicting by recency. However it is for kNN classification/regression on i.i.d.-per-instance streams, not sequence forecasting, and utility/retention decisions are driven by classification-consistency heuristics, not by delayed forecast-error feedback on a deep forecaster.

title: Tackling heterogeneous concept drift with the Self-Adjusting Memory (SAM)
key_mechanism: Extended journal version of SAM-kNN with fuller analysis of the self-adjusting short-/long-term memory architecture.
notes: Extended analysis of SAM; same relevance as above entry.

title: Self-Adjusting Memory: How to Deal with Diverse Drift Types
key_mechanism: Conference companion paper to SAM-kNN.
notes: Duplicate lineage of SAM-kNN; included for completeness.

title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
key_mechanism: Canonical survey of concept-drift adaptation methods including windowing (e.g. ADWIN-style), instance weighting, and ensemble approaches for data-stream learning.
notes: Background reference for ADWIN-style windowing and general drift-adaptation vocabulary.

title: From concept drift to model degradation: An overview on performance-aware drift detectors
key_mechanism: Recent (2022) overview of drift detectors framed around downstream model-performance degradation.
notes: Background/context on performance-aware drift detection relevant to deciding when the forecaster/memory needs adaptation.

title: A survey on machine learning for recurring concept drifting data streams
key_mechanism: Survey specifically on recurring/cyclic concept drift: reviews methods (ensembles, meta-learning, model-based clustering, concept repositories) for detecting when an old regime/concept reappears and reusing prior models/knowledge instead of relearning from scratch.
notes: Directly on-topic for G3e: read abstract in full — confirms recurring-concept handling is an established research theme in the (classification-oriented) data-stream-mining literature, giving vocabulary and precedent (concept repositories / model pools) for a forecasting-memory analogue, but the reviewed methods are for classification/ensemble model-selection, not for retention of raw historical TS segments used as forecast analogues.

title: Handling concept drift via model reuse
key_mechanism: Formalizes reuse of previously-learned models when a recurring or related concept reappears in a drifting stream, choosing which past model(s) to reuse rather than retraining.
notes: Model-level analogue of the 'reuse old regime knowledge instead of evicting it' idea in G3e, but at the level of whole trained models/ensembles, not fine-grained memory segments in a retrieval bank.
